data.title: AM Markets Need to Know: Trump disputes GDP, OPEC pressure, and more
data.description:
Stock index futures surged on Friday as Wall Street looked to close out a volatile week with a winning session, while Treasury yields moved higher following the Thanksgiving holiday break.

Here are the five news items investors should watch:

Trump challenges revised GDP figures: President Donald Trump called for an immediate investigation into the Commerce Department's revised third-quarter GDP figures, alleging that officials deliberately released inaccurate data ahead of the November midterm elections. The department revised annualized economic growth to 4.3% from its initial estimate of 3.4%. Trump described the revision as a "record setting error" but provided no evidence of deliberate manipulation.

U.S. pressured Venezuela and Iraq over OPEC: The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC and blocked Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The pressure targeted two of the cartel's five founding members as Washington sought to encourage greater oil production. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman subsequently intervened to persuade the administration to drop its push against Venezuela.

Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return: President Donald Trump said Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was happy to return to his position, describing the executive's reinstatement as a "second term." Speaking at Mar-a-Lago, Trump defended his intervention despite bipartisan national security concerns. He offered no specific details when asked about the information supporting his confidence in Huang.

School districts push Google to disable AI features: Los Angeles Unified School District has disabled Google's (GOOG) (GOOGL) AI-generated search summaries on school-issued devices, as districts demand permanent opt-out options for educational products. The move makes LAUSD, which serves approximately 500,000 students, the largest district to sideline the feature. The dispute could put pressure on Google's position in the U.S. education market.

Icahn Enterprises faces mounting refinancing pressure: Icahn Enterprises (IEP) faces growing debt concerns after warning that it may not be able to refinance $1.4B of bonds due in May on acceptable terms, or at all. Yields on the bonds have climbed above 14% from ~ 6% three months ago, while some 2029 notes have reportedly topped 30%. Its major holding, CVR Energy (CVI), has also lost approximately 46% since agreeing to acquire two refineries.

data.title: Trump Media to spend up to $13M courting shareholders for TAE merger approval - report
data.description:
Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT), the owner of Truth Social, expects to spend between $8M and $13M, plus additional expenses, on a shareholder solicitation campaign ahead of its proposed merger with fusion energy company TAE Technologies, the Financial Times reported.

The company has hired Alliance Advisors to persuade shareholders to support the all-stock merger, with a shareholder vote scheduled for December 14. Trump Media said reaching more than 600,000 retail shareholders represents a significant undertaking.

The proposed spending has drawn attention because routine proxy solicitation campaigns typically cost less than $1M, according to Michael Levin, a corporate governance expert cited by the report.

Alliance Advisors defended its fees, saying the amount reflects the work involved in reaching Trump Media's shareholder base and is consistent with industry standards.

The merger requires approval from a majority of Trump Media's (DJT) outstanding shares to increase its authorized share capital. The company has warned shareholders that failing to vote will count as opposition to the proposal.

Directors including Donald Trump Jr. and Boris Epshteyn control 42% of the company's stock, the report pointed.

Separately, Trump Media (DJT) has paid $650,000 to social-media marketing firm Outside The Box Capital, which hired online personalities to promote the company and the proposed merger.

The deal would combine Trump Media with TAE Technologies, which reported a net loss of $201M for the year ended March 2026. Trump Media (DJT) shares have fallen nearly 72% so far this year.

data.title: BP and Iberdrola begin operations at Spain hydrogen plant
data.description:
• BP (BP) and Spain’s Iberdrola have begun operations at a 25-MW green hydrogen plant at BP’s Castellón refinery, which the companies describe as Spain’s largest operational facility of its kind.
  • The plant, developed by the 50/50 joint venture and operated by BP, is currently the largest green hydrogen plant operating in Spain.
  • It's expected to produce around 2,800 tonnes of green hydrogen a year. Iberdrola supplies the plant with 170 GWh a year of renewable electricity from its Spanish wind and solar farms under a power purchase agreement.
  • Hydrogen is an essential part of the refining process at Castellón.

data.title: Einride signs electric freight deal with Essity
data.description:
• Stockholm-based autonomous and electric freight firm Einride (ENRD) said on Thursday the global hygiene and health company Essity (ETTYF) has started electric freight operations with ENRD in Sweden.
  • The addition of Essity to Einride’s shipping customers illustrates how retailers and shippers adopt electric freight solutions to combine high operational reliability with lower emissions.
  • "At our Falkenberg site, we are continuously looking for ways to make our operations and transports more efficient while reducing our environmental impact," said Charles El Hajj, Site Director at Essity’s Falkenberg site.
  • ENRD conducts its operations for Essity near residential areas. The operations launched in May are expected to reduce emissions by an estimated 72 tonnes of CO₂e per year.

data.title: Biotest sells European plasma business to Grifols for €220M
data.description:
• Biotest (BIESF) said on Friday it has sold its European plasma collection business to Grifols Worldwide Operations, a subsidiary of Grifols (GRFS), for €220M. 
  • Under a 30-year plasma supply agreement, Grifols will supply Biotest with plasma, supporting long-term supply continuity for Biotest’s manufacturing operations.
  • The transaction also includes Biotest’s European plasma supply agreements with third parties, allowing Grifols to optimize plasma sourcing and capture efficiencies in procurement and supply chain management.
  • Biotest’s 47 plasma donation centers will also be integrated into Grifols’ existing European network, bringing the combined network to 97 sites across Germany, Austria, Hungary and the Czech Republic. A single operating model will enable more coordinated management of plasma collection across Europe.
  • The deal value will be settled by offsetting existing debt owed by Biotest to Grifols and is expected to close on 31 December.
  • GRFS is up 2.67% in pre-market trading.

data.title: CPTPP-ASEAN-EU meet: Stable trade, supply chain resilience in focus
data.description:
The European Union, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) gathered in Vietnam to discuss economic ties and supply chain resilience.

Some of the 14 countries that were targeted with new U.S. tariffs this week were among the participants of the dialogue. These include the EU, Japan, Vietnam, Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia.

"In this time of global trade uncertainty, CPTPP parties and the EU are committed toreinforcing a stable and predictable trade environment," according to a joint statement from the blocs.

Notably, the EU and CPTPP announced a supply chain early warning network that aims to identify supply chain risks earlier, exchange information faster and coordinate responses to disruptions. The network will hold its first meeting in early 2027.

EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the network will help both blocs to "better anticipate disruptions, reduce vulnerabilities and support businesses and citizens who depend on open and reliable trade."

To note, the CPTPP is the successor to the Trans-Pacific Partnership, which was originally led by the U.S. President Trump withdrew from the Pacific Rim trade bloc in 2017.

The CPTPP now comprises the UK, Japan, Australia, Canada, Chile, Vietnam, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Singapore, Brunei and Peru.

Members of the CPTPP and ASEAN also resolved to strengthen supply chain resilience and global value chains through their collective actions, among other commitments.

Separately, the CPTPP agreed to start talks regarding the UAE, Indonesia ‌and the Philippines potentially joining the bloc.

data.title: Zara, H&M shift garment orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest - report
data.description:
Fast fashion brands including Zara (IDEXY) and H&M (HNNMY) have diverted about $254M in garment orders from Bangladesh between November 1 and 18, with most of the orders moving to India, Reuters reported, citing three factory owners.

Marks & Spencer (MAKSY) and French fashion retailer Celio were also among the brands identified in the report. The diverted orders account for nearly a tenth of Bangladesh's monthly orders.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) estimated that labour unrest has caused more than $400M in production losses. Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers this week, triggering fresh clashes with police after workers demanded more than double their existing wages.

India, Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia are attracting orders as manufacturers in Bangladesh face labour unrest, higher wages, energy shortages and rising production costs.

India offers buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can reduce lead times by up to 15 days, according to M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA.

Zara parent Inditex (IDEXY), H&M (HNNMY), Marks & Spencer (MAKSY) and Celio did not immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's requests for comment.

data.title: Biggest stock movers Friday: SPCX, PHAR, VRTX, ALVO, and more
data.description:
U.S. stock futures climbed Friday as markets reopened after Thanksgiving, building on a late-Wednesday dip-buying fueled by renewed momentum in the AI trade.

Here are some of Friday’s biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

SpaceX (SPCX) +6% - Shares moved higher and drew the spotlight in premarket trading, up 4% after Elon Musk pledged to personally match SpaceX's share contribution for eligible American children's Trump Accounts (potentially topping ~$18.4B across ~72M U.S. children). Separately, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell pledged to donate more than 2M shares, though distribution details were not disclosed.

PHAR (Pharming Group) +17.11% - Shares plunged ~17% after temporarily pausing Ruconest manufacturing due to a media fill simulation failure at a third-party fill-finish manufacturer, though shares are surging in premarket trading, with existing supply running through mid-December and no other medicines affected.

KNTK (Kinetik Holdings) +7.07% - Shares jumped premarket on a Bloomberg report that Targa Resources is in talks to acquire the ~$8.9B pipeline operator, though no deal is finalized and standalone or rival-bid scenarios remain possible.

Biggest stock losers

Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) -7.3% - Shares slid ~8% after-hours and were down in premarket trading on the FDA's three-month delay for rival povetacicept, easing near-term competitive pressure on Vera's approved IgAN drug, Trutakna.

ALVO (Alvotech)  -9.9% - Shares face pressure after a federal court granted Janssen a preliminary injunction on proposed Simponi/Simponi Aria biosimilar AVT05 over a single filtration manufacturing patent, which Alvotech plans to appeal while citing strong demand.

data.title: Amadeus secures multi-year distribution agreement with Türkiye's Pegasus Airlines
data.description:
• Spanish technology company Amadeus IT Group (AMADF) signed a multi-year distribution agreement with Pegasus Airlines, a Turkish low-cost carrier, to make the airline's New Distribution Capability (NDC) fares and ancillary services available to travel sellers worldwide.
  • Under the agreement, travel agencies connected to Amadeus will gain access to Pegasus' NDC offers, including fares and additional services such as baggage, seat selection and inflight meals.
  • The deal will also bring all content Pegasus makes available through its direct-connect channel to Amadeus' distribution network.
  • The partnership aims to expand Pegasus' reach across international travel sales channels and give travel sellers access to a broader range of the airline's offerings.
  • The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

data.title: Coca-Cola HBC completes acquisition of 75% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa
data.description:
• The Coca-Cola Company (KO) (CCHBF) and Gutsche Family Investments, or GFI, said on Friday the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa, or CCBA, to bottling partner Coca-Cola HBC has been completed.
  • As part of the deal, KO sold 41.52% of its 66.52% stake in CCBA to Coca-Cola HBC, while Coca-Cola HBC acquired the 33.48% stake held by GFI.
  • The companies have also set up a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in CCBA, held by KO, within a six-year period.
  • This transaction highlights KO's ongoing strategy to rebrand company-owned and controlled bottling operations. The Gutsche family will remain connected to the Coca-Cola system and Africa through its ownership stake in Coca-Cola HBC.
